setup.title: Welcome to MoonlightWeb
setup.intro: Let's finish setting up MoonlightWeb on this computer.
setup.internetBody: MoonlightWeb can allow streaming from outside your local network. Your router is asked (UPnP) to open a streaming port during each session, and whoever connects reaches this PC directly — each side of a peer-to-peer connection sees the other's public IP address. This PC holds one outgoing connection to the MoonlightWeb introduction server, which sees its public IP address and when it is online, and asks a MoonlightWeb STUN server what that public address is; if that server cannot be reached, a public one (Google, Cloudflare) is tried instead. No public DNS record is created, no certificate is issued for this machine, and ports 80/443 stay closed. You can turn this off at any time from the Admin page.
setup.sunshinePaired: Sunshine is installed and paired with MoonlightWeb.
setup.sunshineInstalled: Sunshine is already installed. Enter its credentials so MoonlightWeb can pair with it.
setup.sunshineNotDetected: Sunshine was not detected. Install it automatically, then set the credentials MoonlightWeb will use to pair.
setup.sunshineManual: Sunshine was not detected. Please install Sunshine manually, then reopen this page to pair.
setup.credsRequired: Please enter the Sunshine username and password so MoonlightWeb can pair automatically.
setup.sunshineCredsWrong: Sunshine refused these credentials. Check the username and password of its web interface (https://localhost:47990), or click "Skip for now" to pair later.
setup.sunshineUnreachable: Sunshine is installed but is not answering on this machine. Start it, then try again — or click "Skip for now" to pair later.
setup.displayBody: Sunshine can only stream a screen that is switched on. Once this machine blanks its display, there are no frames to capture and every stream fails — even from an unlocked session. Locking the screen stays fine.
setup.displayOption: Never let this machine's display blank or sleep
setup.displayAlreadyAwake: This machine's display is already set never to blank or sleep.
setup.displayFailed: The display setting could not be applied ({{error}}) — set "Blank Screen" to Never in your desktop's Power settings.
setup.autostartOption: Launch MoonlightWeb automatically when you log in
setup.autostartInstalled: MoonlightWeb already starts automatically at login.
setup.donePermissions: One last step: open Sunshine and grant it Screen Recording and Accessibility permissions in System Settings — macOS requires you to do this manually.
setup.sunshineInstallFailed: Sunshine installation failed: {{error}}. Try again (you'll be asked for your password), uncheck Sunshine, or skip this step.

selfStream.title: Streaming your own PC?
selfStream.body: You're about to stream the very computer you're sitting at. The Inception effect is fun and all, but MoonlightWeb is way more useful when you stream this PC from another device. Quick reminder: MoonlightWeb installs on the PC you want to stream, not the one you play on 😉

stats.title: Help decide what MoonlightWeb supports next
stats.body: MoonlightWeb can send anonymous statistics about your streams, so the project knows what people actually use. Nothing identifies you or your machine, and refusing changes nothing: streaming, updates and every feature work exactly the same.
stats.sentIntro: Sent when a stream starts and ends:
stats.statsSent2: bitrate range and the connection type used
stats.statsSent3: whether the viewer was on your network or the Internet, and the kind of device (computer, phone, tablet, TV)
stats.statsSent4: how long the session lasted, and the MoonlightWeb version and operating system
stats.statsNever1: the name of your PC, your account, or any password or key
stats.statsNever2: which game or application you launch
stats.statsNever3: your IP address — it is never stored, only turned into a number that changes every day
stats.necessary: This is not about cookies: the sign-in cookie the application needs to work is unaffected, and so is the separate Internet Access agreement you may have already given.
stats.thanks: Thank you — statistics are on. You can turn them off any time in Settings.
stats.saveFailed: Your answer could not be saved — nothing is being sent.
stats.toggle: Send anonymous statistics about my streams
stats.toggleDesc: Resolution, frame rate, codec, connection type and session length — never your PC name, your account, what you launch, or your IP address. Turning this off stops it immediately; nothing else changes.
stats.unavailable: This build does not report statistics.
stats.ownerOnly: Only the machine this runs on can change that answer.
stats.playerCookies: This page keeps two things in your browser, and both are needed for it to work: the invitation you unlocked with the PIN, and the options you pick here (screen size, controls). There is no advertising or tracking cookie, and nothing is shared with anyone else.
stats.playerStatsOn: The computer you are joining reports anonymous statistics about the session it runs for you. It is its owner’s choice, not yours to make — but here is exactly what it covers.
stats.playerStatsOff: The computer you are joining reports nothing at all about this session.

settings.title: Streaming Settings
settings.resolutionDesc: Resolution of the stream sent over the network.
settings.frameRateDesc: A higher frame rate helps reduce latency but needs more bandwidth.
settings.hdrDesc: High Dynamic Range — richer colors and contrast.
settings.hdrNoWebgpu: Unavailable: this browser/device has no WebGPU, the stream stays SDR.
settings.chroma444Desc: Full-resolution color (4:4:4) instead of 4:2:0. Requires both the host AND client GPU to support 4:4:4 for the chosen codec. Needs significantly higher bandwidth.
settings.tearingDesc: Disables VSync for slightly lower latency; may cause image tearing.
settings.muteHostDesc: Mute the host PC speakers while streaming. Audio is still sent to this device.
settings.bitrateDesc: Auto-adjusted from resolution, frame rate and HDR.
settings.videoEnhancementDesc: Leverages hardware acceleration to improve picture clarity by upscaling when stream resolution is below your display resolution.
settings.webgpuUnavailable: WebGPU is not available in this browser — video enhancement is disabled.
settings.videoEnhancementHdrNote: With HDR, the stream is tone-mapped to SDR (ACES) before enhancement — uses software AV1 decoding, slightly heavier on the CPU.
settings.videoCodecDesc: HEVC for best balance of quality and compatibility.
settings.codecFallback: {{selected}} was selected but is not supported by this browser. Falling back to {{effective}}.
settings.noCodecSupportedBody: This browser does not support H.264, HEVC, or AV1 decoding. Streaming is not possible.
settings.showPerfStatsDesc: Overlays FPS, bitrate, frame loss and latency stats during streaming.
settings.gamingModeDesc: Captures the mouse and every keystroke — even the Windows key — for a native-like experience. Only the exit shortcut stays on this device.
settings.touchScreenDesc: Tap directly where you want on the picture (absolute) instead of the relative trackpad model. A 1-finger drag then scrolls, in any direction.
settings.pointerSensitivityDesc: Trackpad/touch cursor speed (higher = faster pointer movement).
settings.resetDefaultsDesc: Restore all streaming settings to their default values.
settings.logoutDesc: Ends this browser's session and stops any running stream. The next visit from this device asks for a PIN again. Your other devices stay signed in.
settings.logoutConfirm: Log out of this server? Any running stream stops and this device will need a new PIN to come back.
settings.powerSaveDesc: Forces the lightest pipeline on battery: native video transport (UDP first), H.264, no HDR, no enhancement, 720p / 60fps. Resolution, frame rate and bitrate stay adjustable. Unchecking restores your previous values if you didn't change them.
settings.languageDesc: Interface language. The page reloads when you change it.

admin.title: Server Settings
admin.hostOnly: Server administration is only available from the machine hosting the server.
admin.accessPinDesc: Share this PIN with remote users to grant them access to this server. The PIN is valid for one session only.
admin.pinConsumedHint: The previous PIN was used by a remote user. Generate a new PIN to allow another session.
admin.activeSessionsDesc: Remote users currently connected to this server.
admin.certAuthDesc: When enabled, remote users can upload a certificate file instead of entering a PIN. The certificate is a long random token that never changes — generate it once and share it securely.
admin.downloadCertHint: The certificate grants the same access as a PIN. Share it only with trusted users. If compromised, use the "Generate" button below to issue a new one.
admin.remoteAdminEnable: Allow administration from the local network
admin.remoteAdminDesc: Lets you open this page from another computer on your local network, using a password. This machine never needs it, and the password is never accepted from the internet.
admin.remoteAdminNoPassword: No password has been set yet, so no computer on your network can open this page. Choose one below to allow it.
admin.remoteAdminCustom: Your own password is in use.
admin.remoteAdminHint: Changing the password immediately signs out every computer that used the old one.
admin.remoteAdminTooShort: The password must be at least {{count}} characters.
admin.unlockDesc: This page is normally reserved for the machine hosting the server. Enter the administration password to open it from here.
admin.unlockDefaultHint: If it was never changed, use the default password from the MoonlightWeb documentation — then change it right away from this page.
admin.unlockLockout: Too many attempts — try again in {{seconds}}s.
admin.internetInfo1: By enabling Internet Access, you allow MoonlightWeb to ask your router (UPnP) to open a streaming port during each session. Whoever connects reaches this PC directly — each side of a peer-to-peer connection sees the other's public IP address. This PC holds one outgoing connection to the MoonlightWeb introduction server, which sees its public IP address and when it is online, and asks a MoonlightWeb STUN server what that public address is; if that server cannot be reached, a public one (Google, Cloudflare) is tried instead. No public DNS record is created, no certificate is issued for this machine, and ports 80/443 stay closed. You can turn this off at any time from the Admin page.
admin.internetInfoLegacy: By enabling Internet Access, you authorize sending this server's public IP address to PowerDNS to create an A record pointing to your network.
admin.legacySunset: This instance still holds the sub-domain {{domain}}, served by the shared MoonlightWeb DNS service. That service shuts down in February 2027 and the sub-domain stops working then. It is no longer shown as an address because the link above has replaced it — that one is not affected.
admin.rendezvousReady: This address reaches this machine from anywhere. It is not published anywhere else — copy it to the devices you want to stream from.
admin.rendezvousOffline: The line to the introduction server is down, so this address will not answer until it comes back. It is still the right address.
admin.rendezvousReplaces: This is your machine's address now. It is published nowhere else — copy it to the devices you stream from. Your older sub-domain keeps working until that service shuts down in February 2027, and is no longer shown here.
admin.consentRequired: The Internet link is paused: the permission you gave earlier described the former mechanism (public DNS record and certificate), which no longer applies to this installation. Read the description above, then tick the box again to re-enable the link under the current terms.
admin.upnpAvailableNote: Authorizes UPnP port mapping on your router (available on this network). You can also forward ports manually.
admin.upnpUnavailableNote: Authorizes UPnP port mapping on your router (not available on this network). You can also forward ports manually.
admin.dnsPropagating: DNS propagation in progress — your site will be available shortly. This may take a few minutes...
admin.portMappingHint: UPnP is not available on your router. To allow external access, manually forward ports in your router settings:
admin.portMappingEnterIp: Enter the LAN IP address of this server (e.g. 192.168.1.x) as the destination.
admin.localAccessHint: Access this server from other devices on your local network.
admin.localAccessMulti: The first address is the one on your shared network; the others belong to virtual adapters and only reach their own virtual machines.
admin.transportModeHint: When set to Auto, the system tries the best available protocol (UDP > TCP > WSS) based on network conditions and browser support.
admin.httpsPortDesc: Configure the server HTTPS port. Changes require a brief service interruption while the port is rebound.
admin.confirmRegenCert: Regenerating the certificate will invalidate all existing certificate files. Continue?
admin.portSavedRestart: Port saved to settings. Restart required to apply.
admin.noPinToCopy: No valid PIN to copy — generate one first
admin.pinSelected: PIN selected — press Ctrl+C to copy
admin.dnsPropagated: DNS propagated -- your site is now available at {{domain}}
admin.dnsTimeout: DNS propagation timed out after 5 minutes. Check your domain configuration.
admin.internetNotActive: Internet access is enabled but not active: DNS registration did not complete. Check the PowerDNS token and your network, then re-enable Internet access.
admin.sunshineInstalled: Sunshine is installed on this computer.
admin.sunshineNotInstalled: Sunshine is not installed. Install it to stream games from this computer.
admin.sunshineManual: Sunshine is not installed, and automatic installation is not available on this system. Please install Sunshine manually.
admin.sunshineInstallHint: Your operating system will ask for your account password to install Sunshine.
admin.sunshineCredsRequired: Enter a username and password for Sunshine.
admin.stopSunshineHint: Stops the Sunshine server running on this computer. On macOS it also lives in the top-right menu bar. It restarts at your next login (or launch it from Applications).
admin.startSunshineHint: Starts the Sunshine server on this computer so you can stream from it.
admin.sunshineStopped2: Sunshine is installed but not running.
admin.openSunshineConfigHint: Sunshine has no window: on macOS it runs in the background (top-right menu bar), on Windows/Linux in the tray. Configure it from its web interface. Sign in with the Sunshine username and password you set.
admin.confirmRevoke: Revoke the session of "{{name}}"? That device will have to enter a PIN again.

stream.multiSeatInputWhereUnknown: That interface is at the same address as the host, on the seat's stream port plus one, over https. Sign in there, find this device in the list of paired clients and turn its input permissions on.

videoCapture.title: The host can't capture its screen
videoCapture.bodyRemote: Sunshine on "{{name}}" has no screen to capture. On that machine: wake the display and check it isn't blanked or asleep (a locked session with the screen off produces no frames), or plug in a display / HDMI dummy plug. If "{{name}}" is a Mac, also turn Sunshine on in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Screen Recording and restart Sunshine.
videoCapture.bodyLocal: Sunshine on this machine has no screen to capture. Wake the display and check it isn't blanked or asleep (a locked session with the screen off produces no frames), or plug in a display / HDMI dummy plug, then use "Restart Sunshine & retry" below.
videoCapture.bodyMac: Sunshine on this Mac can't capture the screen. Open System Settings → Privacy & Security → Screen Recording and turn on Sunshine, then use "Restart Sunshine & retry" below (macOS only applies the permission after Sunshine restarts). If there's no display, connect one or use an HDMI dummy plug.
videoCapture.opened: Opened Screen Recording settings on the host.
videoCapture.openFailed: Couldn't open the settings pane — open it manually.
videoCapture.restartFailed: Couldn't restart Sunshine — quit and reopen it manually.

sharing.pinHint: Send the PIN separately from the link - together they let someone in, apart they are useless.
sharing.lanOnly: This link only opens from your own network. Turn on internet access to share it further.
sharing.offline: Your PC is not reachable right now. The link stays valid and will open as soon as it is back.
sharing.exitBody: People are connected through your invitations. What should happen to them?
sharing.exitLeaveDesc: you disconnect, the game keeps running and your players keep playing.
sharing.exitStopDesc: the game closes and every player is disconnected.

warning.desktop: They can use the keyboard and mouse of this PC, but not a gamepad.
warning.full: They control the keyboard and mouse of this PC. Only share this with someone you trust completely.

sharing.regenerateHint: Regenerating a new link disconnects whoever is streaming on the previous one.
sharing.secretsLost: The link and PIN were forgotten when the server restarted. The invitation still works for whoever holds it; regenerate to get a pair you can read.

sharing.appHint: Nothing is running, so the first guest to enter their PIN is what starts this app.
sharing.noApps: This host has no apps to share yet.
sharing.unavailable: Session sharing is not available on this server.

player.immersiveHint: For games: the mouse is locked inside the frame and every keystroke goes to the remote PC.
player.joinFailed: Could not join. Try again in a moment.
player.busy: Someone is already streaming with this invitation. Only one screen at a time.
player.willLaunch: Nothing is running yet. Starting will launch the game you were invited to.
player.willLaunchApp: Nothing is running yet. Starting will launch {{app}} on that PC.

access.viewer: You can watch, but not play.
access.gamer: You can play with a gamepad.
access.full: You have keyboard and mouse control.
access.desktop: You have keyboard and mouse control, but no gamepad.

player.pinBody: The person who invited you sent a 6-digit code along with this link.
player.pinWrong: Wrong code. Check the one you were sent.
player.pinLocked: Too many attempts - try again in {{seconds}}s.
player.deadBody: This invitation has expired, or it was turned off. You have arrived in the void where old game links go.
player.endedBody: Your host stopped the game, so the stream stopped with it. Nothing broke - you were just unplugged.
player.endedHint: Give them a ring and ask for a new link.
player.appGone: The app this invitation was made for is no longer on the host. Ask for a new link.
player.alreadyBound: This invitation is already tied to another machine. Ask for a fresh link.

backend.instruction: Point MoonlightWeb at this host’s control API. Saving pairs straight away, so players never have to enter a PIN.
backend.willIdentify: Give the address of this host’s control API and MoonlightWeb will work out what it is. Nothing else is needed.
backend.tokenKeep: Leave empty to keep the stored token
backend.ready: Saving will register the backend and pair with it.
backend.urlRequired: A control API URL is required.
backend.typesFailed: Could not load the list of backend types.
backend.capProvisioning: Seats can be created on demand
backend.seatsUnsupported: This backend does not expose seats.
backend.seatAccountPrompt: Which account should this seat use?
backend.seatProvisioning: Creating the seat… this can take a minute.
backend.pairPasswordPlaceholder: Password for the seat web UI
backend.pairHint: MultiSeat cannot pair a seat through its own API, so MoonlightWeb pushes the PIN to each seat’s Apollo web interface. These are the credentials you set there — one pair covers every seat.
backend.seatFreeHint: Release this seat from its owner, keeping the seat itself
backend.seatFreed: Seat released — it can be claimed again.
